editorial.headline: Used Personal Goods: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retail trade in pre-owned watches, wall clocks and jewellery is nationally open to foreign ownership, yet Bali’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for it.
editorial.body:
This activity is the retail trade in used personal goods. Its stated examples—pre-owned watches, wall clocks and jewellery—give the category a clear centre of gravity: personal articles being sold again at retail. The scope identifies a particular trade in personal equipment, rather than a generic label for second-hand commerce. The result is a concise, recognisable activity for businesses whose offer is built around those pre-owned personal items. That clarity matters when reading the foreign-investment position, because the national and Bali determinations attach to this defined retail scope.

The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. At national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Plainly put, the national position allows a fully foreign-owned PMA registration for this activity. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Yet neither a complete national ownership allowance nor the availability of each listed scale answers the Bali question. Bali is assessed separately in the record, and its finding changes the practical outcome for a PMA applicant on the island.

That Bali outcome is direct: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali entry marks it blocked on risk-class grounds. For the Besar scale, the record says every scope has OSS risk assessed as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for activities with Low or Medium-Low risk. The stated reason ties this activity to that moratorium in May 2026. There is no Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage in the record; the restriction stated here is a block on PMA registration.

The honest account therefore needs both levels in view. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA with 100% foreign ownership, across the listed scales. In Bali, the national ceiling does not displace the island-wide moratorium: its status is blocked for PMA registration. Calling it simply open would omit the provincial block; calling it simply closed would erase the national allowance. The accurate reading is a nationally open retail activity whose PMA route is closed in Bali under the recorded risk-class moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not displace Bali’s permanent island-wide moratorium on PMA registration.
